title: Drawing, Observation & Creative Calling
purpose: Use one major weekly theme to inspire creative work, teach a foundational visual-art concept, and produce one focused studio project that becomes evidence of growth.

design_rules.interface: centered symmetrical single-column progression; charcoal accordion bars; crisp cream cards; parchment/khaki accents; 7px corners; no text below 16px
design_rules.mastery: All required inputs and evidence complete plus objective knowledge check >=80%; artistic taste is never objectively scored.
design_rules.vocabulary: Populate the universal Higher Learning vocabulary engine from curriculum terms; do not duplicate a vocabulary runtime.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Artists grow by preserving process, experiments, revisions and finished work—not only polished outcomes.
weeks.foundational_skill: Observation, documentation and baseline self-assessment
weeks.monday_project: Create a baseline observation drawing and establish the first portfolio record.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Slow looking can reveal edges, overlaps and relationships that symbols and memory usually simplify.
weeks.foundational_skill: Contour, edge awareness and sustained observation
weeks.monday_project: Create two contour studies of one observed subject, including one slow continuous or modified-contour drawing.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Accuracy grows from comparing relationships rather than naming or guessing individual parts.
weeks.foundational_skill: Relative measurement, angle comparison and proportion
weeks.monday_project: Create a measured observational drawing using comparative width, height and angle checks.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Light turns flat shapes into convincing form through organized value relationships.
weeks.foundational_skill: Value grouping, light logic and form modeling
weeks.monday_project: Create a five-value study that turns simple observed objects into believable three-dimensional forms.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Color changes dramatically when hue, lightness and intensity are controlled independently.
weeks.foundational_skill: Hue, value and saturation control
weeks.monday_project: Create a small color study in three variations that alter value or saturation while keeping the core subject consistent.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A color is never experienced alone; neighboring colors can intensify, quiet or redirect attention.
weeks.foundational_skill: Complementary, analogous and temperature relationships
weeks.monday_project: Create two versions of one composition using contrasting color relationships and compare their visual effect.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Color carries environmental, material, personal and cultural associations that shift by context.
weeks.foundational_skill: Contextual color observation and responsible interpretation
weeks.monday_project: Create a place-based color study using an observed palette and a short note separating observation from personal/cultural interpretation.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Artists can guide attention by controlling contrast, scale, placement, detail and quiet space.
weeks.foundational_skill: Hierarchy, focal point and emphasis
weeks.monday_project: Create three thumbnails with different focal strategies, then develop one into a resolved composition.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Visual weight can feel stable or dynamic without requiring perfect symmetry.
weeks.foundational_skill: Symmetrical/asymmetrical balance, directional movement and visual weight
weeks.monday_project: Create two compositions from the same elements—one stable and one intentionally dynamic.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Arrangement, viewpoint, sequence and symbol can imply events without explaining everything in words.
weeks.foundational_skill: Narrative composition, viewpoint and sequencing
weeks.monday_project: Create a single-image visual narrative with a clear before/now/after implication or story tension.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Construction and gesture can support accuracy without stripping a drawing of life.
weeks.foundational_skill: Construction shapes, gesture and observational structure
weeks.monday_project: Create an observed object study beginning with gesture and construction lines, then refine selected contours.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Cast shadow, core shadow and reflected light reveal both the object and the space around it.
weeks.foundational_skill: Light direction, shadow families and volume
weeks.monday_project: Create a controlled light study of one or more simple forms with clearly organized light and shadow.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Gesture and spatial relationships can communicate movement without relying on stereotypes or facial detail.
weeks.foundational_skill: Figure gesture, proportion and spatial placement
weeks.monday_project: Create a short series of timed figure or pose studies, then one longer expressive figure-in-space composition.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Perspective is one useful system for organizing depth, not the only valid way artists create space.
weeks.foundational_skill: Horizon line, vanishing points, convergence and overlap
weeks.monday_project: Create an interior or exterior spatial drawing using observational or one-/two-point perspective.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Changing viewpoint changes what information a drawing reveals about a structure.
weeks.foundational_skill: Plan, elevation, perspective and viewpoint comparison
weeks.monday_project: Draw one simple architectural subject from at least two distinct viewpoints or projection methods.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A designed environment can carry story through scale, light, depth, pathways and placement.
weeks.foundational_skill: Spatial storytelling and environmental composition
weeks.monday_project: Design an imagined or observed environment in which space itself helps communicate a narrative.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Repeated forms, intervals and contrast can choreograph how the eye moves through an image.
weeks.foundational_skill: Rhythm, balance, hierarchy and negative space
weeks.monday_project: Create a composition using a repeated motif, a clear focal point and intentionally shaped negative space.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Variation inside repetition can make a pattern feel alive rather than mechanical.
weeks.foundational_skill: Motif development, repetition, interval and transformation
weeks.monday_project: Develop one motif into a pattern sequence that visibly changes rhythm or direction.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Art can communicate intentionally when image, text, hierarchy and audience are considered together.
weeks.foundational_skill: Message, hierarchy, image/text integration and audience
weeks.monday_project: Create a small poster or visual message that combines imagery and limited text for a defined audience.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Every material leaves a different record of pressure, speed, direction and surface.
weeks.foundational_skill: Mark-making, material testing and texture
weeks.monday_project: Build a texture atlas using several accessible tools or materials, then use selected marks in an original study.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Layering changes not only surface but also meaning, sequence and relationships between images.
weeks.foundational_skill: Cutting, layering, adhesion, transparency/opacity and attribution
weeks.monday_project: Create an original collage or mixed-media composition using at least three intentional layers.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Light behaves differently when an artwork physically rises from the surface.
weeks.foundational_skill: Low relief, tactile/implied texture and structural revision
weeks.monday_project: Create a safe low-relief surface study, photograph it under two lighting conditions, then revise one structural choice.

weeks.inspiration_lens: In printmaking, the spaces removed, retained and reversed become equally important.
weeks.foundational_skill: Figure/ground, positive/negative shape and mirror reversal
weeks.monday_project: Design a simple two-value print matrix or safe paper/foam equivalent that depends on clear positive/negative shapes.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Repetition reveals both control and difference; an edition can preserve consistency while allowing intentional variation.
weeks.foundational_skill: Registration, pressure, repeatability and edition documentation
weeks.monday_project: Produce a small edition or simulated edition of repeated impressions and document one controlled variation.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Printed images have long carried messages into public spaces because they can be reproduced and distributed.
weeks.foundational_skill: Message design, audience and reproducible image planning
weeks.monday_project: Create a message-based print or printable graphic series with a clearly identified audience and responsible claim.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A photograph records a framed selection, not the whole truth of a situation.
weeks.foundational_skill: Framing, viewpoint, light and evidence limits
weeks.monday_project: Create a six-image framing study of one subject that demonstrates how camera position and crop change interpretation.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Sequence and captions can clarify evidence—or distort it—so context and consent matter.
weeks.foundational_skill: Visual sequencing, caption accuracy, consent and context
weeks.monday_project: Create a responsible six-frame documentary sequence or drawn alternative with accurate contextual captions.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A photo essay gains meaning from selection, order, pacing and revision rather than from isolated images alone.
weeks.foundational_skill: Editing, sequencing, captioning and visual cohesion
weeks.monday_project: Create and revise a short photo essay or drawn visual essay with 5–8 images and concise captions.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Letters are visual forms, but communication fails when expressive choices overwhelm readability.
weeks.foundational_skill: Letterform, spacing, hierarchy and legibility
weeks.monday_project: Create an original lettering study and use it in a small title, sign or typographic composition tested for readability.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A grid can organize complexity while still leaving room for contrast, rhythm and surprise.
weeks.foundational_skill: Grid structure, alignment, spacing and modular layout
weeks.monday_project: Design two one-page layouts from the same content using different grid systems, then refine the clearer version.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Information graphics combine visual hierarchy with an obligation to represent evidence honestly.
weeks.foundational_skill: Data/claim hierarchy, scale, sourcing and uncertainty
weeks.monday_project: Create a small evidence-grounded infographic or visual explainer with sources and clearly labeled uncertainty or limits.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Artwork belongs to histories, communities and material traditions that deserve careful sourcing rather than stereotype.
weeks.foundational_skill: Contextual research, attribution and comparative visual analysis
weeks.monday_project: Study two sourced artworks from different contexts and create an original response work that identifies influence without imitation.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Design improves when the artist understands the people, place, need and constraints behind the request.
weeks.foundational_skill: Creative brief, audience needs, feedback and revision
weeks.monday_project: Write a small community/client-style creative brief and produce a first visual proposal followed by one documented revision.

weeks.inspiration_lens: Curating creates meaning through selection, sequence, labels, spacing and accessibility.
weeks.foundational_skill: Selection criteria, sequencing, wall text and exhibition planning
weeks.monday_project: Curate a miniature exhibition of 5–8 works or studies and create a simple floor/page plan with labels.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A capstone asks the artist to choose a question and synthesize techniques rather than merely repeat assignments.
weeks.foundational_skill: Independent inquiry, proposal, iteration and synthesis
weeks.monday_project: Propose and begin an original capstone artwork combining at least three techniques or concepts from the course.

weeks.inspiration_lens: A professional portfolio explains growth through selected evidence, thoughtful sequence and an artist's own reasoning.
weeks.foundational_skill: Curation, presentation, artist statement and defense
weeks.monday_project: Finalize a curated portfolio exhibition and prepare a concise written or oral defense of choices, revisions and future direction.
